newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gold prosecutor quits after attacks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gold prosecutor quits after attacks.

text.p: An Argentine prosecutor investigating a $70 million gold export scam on Friday said he was quitting after he and his sister suffered brutal razor and knife attacks.
Prosecutor Pablo Lanusse told a radio interviewer crime rings "have caused me and all my family a great moral and physical exhaustion."

Lanusse was beaten and slashed on his face and body in October and February by unknown assailants. His sister was attacked in June and forced to carve the word "oro" -- Spanish for gold -- on her own forehead with a knife.
Bomb threats were also made against his son's kindergarten and a school attended by his nephews.
Lanusse said he had requested a transfer to a calmer office so that he and his family may live a normal life.
The prosecutor has led since last year a probe into the activities of 19 companies which allegedly made false claims for $70 million in export subsidies for gold products.

However, Lanusse said his decision was not a defeat and insisted he still trusted in Argentina's justice system, which has recently been under heavy fire by critics, including former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo.

"It was not the mafia, if it can be called so, which dictated the timing" for his departure, the prosecutor said. He said he waited until the case was well under way and 62 people were summoned to testify before requesting a transfer.
"I still believe in justice, in the many judges and prosecutors and employees who do a very good job," he said.
Cavallo, who returned Argentina to a path of economic growth and currency stability, recently accused two ministers of manipulating judges and blocking corruption investigations.
In October, three months after being fired by Menem, he accused Interior Minister Carlos Corach of trying to remove Lanusse from the gold case to stonewall investigators.
